description: Reasoning vault aligned with OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §3.6: graph absolute value functions and solve absolute value equations, including branch and solution-count checks.

archetypes.name: Graph and Read Absolute Value Transformations
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §3.6 — Graphing an Absolute Value Function
archetypes.coreConcept: In g(x)=a|x-h|+k, the corner is (h,k), the sign of a selects the opening direction, and |a| sets the arm slope.
archetypes.mentalModel: Track the corner first, then use one point to set the arm steepness and the sign to choose the opening direction.

cognitiveTraps.description: Reading |x-h| as a shift left by h instead of right by h.
Ignoring a negative outside factor and drawing an upward-opening graph.

archetypes.name: Solve Absolute Value Equations
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §3.6 — Solving an Absolute Value Equation
archetypes.coreConcept: For |A(x)|=B, a negative B gives no real solutions; for nonnegative B, solve A(x)=B and A(x)=-B and report every valid input.
archetypes.mentalModel: An absolute value is a distance: a positive distance can come from two directions, zero from one point, and a negative distance from none.

cognitiveTraps.description: Solving only A(x)=B and omitting the negative branch.
Creating two branches even when the isolated absolute value equals a negative number.

archetypes.figureNone: This archetype solves a symbolic equation by splitting into cases; the equation and branch algebra provide all needed information without a graph.

archetypes.name: Infer an Absolute Value Rule from a Vertex and Point
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §3.6 — Writing an Equation for an Absolute Value Function Given a Graph
archetypes.coreConcept: The vertex determines h and k in a|x-h|+k; a second point determines the scale and whether the graph opens up or down.
archetypes.mentalModel: Place the corner first, then substitute a known point to solve for the signed arm slope.

cognitiveTraps.description: Using the vertex output k as the arm scale instead of solving from the second point.
Using a point's signed horizontal distance instead of its absolute distance from the vertex.

figureBuilders.title: Absolute value rule from a point

archetypes.name: Check Branches in Absolute Value Equations
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §3.6 — Solutions to Absolute Value Equations
archetypes.coreConcept: When the right side depends on x, each candidate from the two algebraic branches must still satisfy the original equation and its nonnegative-distance condition.
archetypes.mentalModel: Split the cases, solve each candidate, then substitute candidates back into the original equation to rule out invalid branches.

cognitiveTraps.description: Keeping an algebraic branch candidate even though the equation's right side is negative there.
cognitiveTraps.trapFormula: x 	ext{ solves a branch but } B(x)<0 ↦ 	ext{keep }x

cognitiveTraps.description: Checking one branch candidate but leaving the other untested in the original equation.

archetypes.figureNone: This archetype focuses on checking algebraic candidates against the original equation; direct substitution and the sign condition are sufficient.

archetypes.name: Solve Absolute Value Inequalities as Intervals
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §3.6 — Absolute Value Functions (distance inequality extension)
archetypes.coreConcept: For a nonnegative bound c, |A(x)|≤c describes inputs whose signed expression lies between -c and c; the solution set is an interval or union of intervals.
archetypes.mentalModel: Translate the absolute distance into matching lower and upper bounds, solve the compound inequality, and preserve inclusive or exclusive endpoints.

cognitiveTraps.description: Keeping only the upper half of the compound inequality and omitting the lower-side solutions.
Using open endpoints for a non-strict inequality or closed endpoints for a strict inequality.

archetypes.figureNone: A number-line figure showing the interval would directly reveal the requested interval answer; the algebraic compound inequality contains the needed structure.
